analysis.title: Is the correction complete?
key_insights: Last week saw sharp global equity losses: S&P 500 -8.61%, Nasdaq 100 -10.43%, Nikkei 225 -7.70%, STOXX 600 -5.17%, SMI -3.53%, iShares MSCI EM ETF -11.62%. US declines were the sharpest weekly drops since the pandemic and April 2025 tariff sell-offs.

S&P 500 base case of an extended wave (3) with 161.8% projection at 7,744 is invalidated. The index broke below 7,493 and the rising 200-day SMA, so wave (3) may have ended near 7,744 and a wave (4) correction is under way.
S&P 500 key support is 6,910-6,817 (6,817 is the 23.6% retracement of wave 3). A break below 6,817 opens 6,182. A recovery above the 200-day SMA is needed for initial stabilisation.

The decline from the 7,845 bull-trap high may be a five-wave impulse: wave 1 to 7,330, wave 2 to 7,656, wave 3 to about 6,910. A tactical wave 4 rebound could retest 7,267-7,350, with a wave 5 decline still possible.

Breadth shows no capitulation: only 5.57% of S&P constituents are at 52-week lows and 10.16% have 14-day RSI below 30, both well below the 2022 and April 2025 extremes. A local low may form but there is no clear evidence of a major low.
Nasdaq 100 broke below 26,200-26,400 and the 23.6% Fibonacci level. Next support is 23,369 and the 200-day SMA at 28,073 is resistance. Weekly RSI is near 40.

Mag-7 (BM7P) broke below 32,600-32,800 and fell to the 38.2% Fibonacci level. Resistance is 32,750 (200-day SMA) and 34,250, with long-term support at 27,920 a possibility. RSI broke support in place since 2025.
SOX fell below its 200-day SMA for the first time since March 2025. It failed at 10,660 and 10,900, and 8,400-8,500 is the next support.
STOXX 600 is holding near its rising 200-day SMA around 629. A weekly close above RSI resistance could bring 745 into focus.
SMI is retesting the 14,669-14,594 breakout area and is a relative outperformer. Holding keeps 15,151 and then 15,760-16,185 in play, while a break below 14,594 targets 14,380 and 14,106.
DAX reversed from 27,329-27,919 and fell below 25,624, weakening the wave 3 scenario. Supports are 24,852 and 23,429.
Nikkei 225 shows possible bullish divergence at 56,899-56,437 support. Recovery above 59,332 and the 200-day SMA near 62,265 would confirm, while a break below 56,437 targets 51,914.

Hang Seng broke below 22,742-22,990 and its 2024 trendline, with 21,425 (50% retracement) next. EEM broke short-term support, with 52.53 the first support in the 50-55 zone, and stays fragile below 60.50.

US 10-year yield stays in a positive structure above 4.80%, with resistance at 5.03% and 5.17%. A break below 4.80% targets 4.62%. Pictet reads this as the bond market viewing the sell-off as consolidation, not a macro breakdown.
Gold faces a push-and-pull: yields above 4.80% and deleveraging favour consolidation, while equity volatility, inflation risks and possible lower yields give structural support.

sector_views.rationale: SOX is below its 200-day SMA for the first time since March 2025 and failed at 10,660-10,900, with 8,400-8,500 possible.
BM7P and Nasdaq 100 broke key supports and are technically weaker below 32,600-32,800.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Holding 4.80% implies consolidation in the equity sell-off. A break targets 4.62% and could support gold.

risk_factors: Absence of broad-based capitulation means a durable low is not confirmed and a wave 5 decline remains possible.
Hawkish Fed policy concerns, the AI trade unwind and weak post-IPO momentum could extend losses.
Yields holding above 4.80% and cross-asset deleveraging may pressure gold and risk assets.
vol_and_positioning: Breadth is not at capitulation: 5.57% of S&P constituents at 52-week lows and 10.16% with 14-day RSI below 30.
Cross-asset signals suggest risk-off positioning has yet to reach clear capitulation.
S&P 500 is deeply oversold short term, leaving scope for a tactical rebound.
